**What happened.** On Friday 11-20 an AI-stock rout hit the whole chip group.
- The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 10.73%, with all 30 members down. The Nasdaq fell 5.28% and the S&P 500 fell 3.70% (TradingKey market wrap).
- Triggers cited were Nvidia down as much as 13% after Reuters reported an SEC review of its accounting, the Anthropic IPO giving back its first-day gains, a new export-license rule for AI chips, and macro nerves.
- TXN fell 7.57% in that wrap, which fits your 7.7%. By that account it did better than the group.
- I found no TXN-specific news or analyst downgrade this week. TradingKey's separate TXN note blames analog inventory digestion and margin worries, but it reads auto-generated and contradicts the company's own results, so I gave it little weight. Its figures also don't match the other reports.

**Fundamentals (Q3 report, 10-21, company release).**
- Revenue was $6.06B, up 28% year over year and 11% from the prior quarter. EPS was $2.62, up 77%, and it beat consensus of about $2.40.
- Analog revenue rose 32% and Embedded Processing rose 21%.
- Operating margin was 47.5%, against 35.1% a year earlier (StockStory call summary).
- On the call, data center revenue nearly doubled, industrial grew over 40% and passed its pre-pandemic peak, and auto grew in the mid-teens.
- The Q4 guide was revenue of $5.80B to $6.30B and EPS of $2.45 to $2.79, both above consensus.
- Trailing free cash flow was $8.4B, though $1.6B of it was CHIPS Act incentives that may not recur (24/7 Wall St.).
- The quarterly dividend was raised 7% to $1.52, which is about a 2.3% yield at 263.75.

**Valuation and risks.**
- The stock trades at about 26 times forward earnings by one count (TradingKey puts it at 34 to 38 times), after a 52-week high near $334.
- Capex is $2B to $3B this year. Fab ramps in Malaysia and Lehi, rising depreciation and longer tool lead times are the watch items.
- A pending Silicon Labs acquisition, mentioned in one source, is funded partly by a $2B notes offering. I didn't verify it against a primary source.
- The data center boom is exactly what the market is now doubting, and that is the part TXN is exposed to.

**What could move it over the next few sessions.**
- **Sector direction.** The move is almost all beta to semis and AI sentiment. Friday after-hours was up 2.7% to 270.75, which hints at a bounce, but a -10% day in the semiconductor index often follows through before it stabilizes.
- **Nvidia and the SEC review.** Any update on the Nvidia accounting review could swing the whole group.
- **Dated events.** HPE reports Monday 11-23, Dell Tuesday, Deere Wednesday (an industrial read), and Q3 GDP and October PCE come before Thanksgiving. Trading will be thin around the holiday. TXN's own earnings are not until 2027-01-26, so there is no company event in the window.
- **Technical level.** 264.08, the 200-day average, is the line that matters. A hold and bounce fits a panic-flush story, while a break below invites more selling.

**Read.** The thesis intact: a nearly doubled data center business, a recovering industrial business and rising margins did not change on Friday. The risk is that sentiment and positioning keep driving price for a few sessions regardless. This favors a long, bounce-style idea over a short, sized small and with the 200-day average as the stop reference. Chasing the after-hours pop carries gap risk both ways.

- Adjusted EPS was $0.52 against $0.47 expected. GAAP EPS was $0.12.
- Fiscal Q3 revenue guidance is $1.49B to $1.59B, and royalties are expected to grow only in the low single digits. Memory prices are hurting phone sales.
- Data-center royalties roughly doubled. Management expects up to $2B of revenue from its AGI CPU (Arm's own server chip) over fiscal 2027 and 2028. First sales are expected at the end of next year.
- The stock fell about 11-13% on 11-05. Nine firms cut price targets after the report.

**What has driven the stock since:**
- **Chip rout:**
  - 11-16: ARM fell about 8% on a SemiAnalysis cut to AI accelerator growth forecasts and risk-reduction ahead of Nvidia earnings.

- **SoftBank:** It owns about 86% of Arm and had pledged 72% of Arm's shares behind a margin loan. That loan was reported at $25B in September, which I could not confirm from a primary source. SoftBank lost $7.1B last quarter. No margin-call price is published. Forced selling is a tail risk, not a known trigger.
- **Related-party revenue:** Bank of America flagged "circular financing" because Arm depends on SoftBank-linked licensing revenue. That revenue was flat at $424M, while outside customers grew 43%.
- **Insiders:** The CFO and Chief Commercial Officer have sold repeatedly. Sales are small and under pre-set trading plans.

**ZS research, as of Sunday 2026-11-22**

**The story**

The after-hours jump is takeover news, not earnings. After Friday's close, reports said CrowdStrike (CRWD) is negotiating to buy Zscaler. A Stocks Today piece citing Reuters says "two insiders" described the talks. I found no Bloomberg or Reuters original, and no price, premium, or cash-versus-stock split has been reported. The talks could still collapse. Neither company has confirmed anything, and the two did expand a partnership on September 2.

- **Size:** Zscaler's market cap at the close was about $32B. Stocks Today compares that with Google's Wiz deal and Palo Alto's roughly $25B offer for CyberArk.
- **Reaction:** After hours ZS rose 16% to 20% depending on the source (your print is +16.3%). CRWD fell as much as 8%, which one source reads as skepticism about paying for it.
- **Friday's regular session:** ZS fell 5.3% inside a broad AI and tech rout. One source calls it the Nasdaq-100's worst week since 2020, with the S&P 500 in correction and Nvidia down sharply. Palo Alto rose 6.5% on its own acquisition news.

**Underlying business**

- **Q4 FY26 (reported September 3):** Revenue was $898.2M, up 25%, ahead of the $877M consensus. ARR was $3.77B, up 25%, or about 20% excluding the acquired Red Canary business.
- **FY27 guidance:** Revenue and ARR growth of 16.6% to 17.5%, a clear slowdown. Q1 guidance is revenue of $935M to $939M and adjusted EPS of $1.15 to $1.16. Guidance was reaffirmed at the October 6 Investor Day.
- **Other items:** About 3% of staff are being cut, and Q4 free cash flow margin fell to 6.8% from 16% after hardware purchases were pulled forward.
- **AI angle:** Management called AI its biggest tailwind, with security-for-AI bookings up more than 50% quarter on quarter.

- The cash figure includes a $28M temporary payroll-tax benefit, so the underlying number is about $532M.

- Zscaler's market value was about $32B and CrowdStrike's about $235B. ZS was down about 13% year to date. Its 52-week high was $336.27 in November 2025.
- ZS at 226.65 is still well below that high. Any bid premium over a $32B value would have to be large to matter against 194.82.

**Fundamentals, from the company's own releases (Sept 3 and Oct 6, 2026).**
- Q4 FY26 revenue was $898.2M, up 25%. Excluding the Red Canary acquisition, FY26 growth was 20%.
- ARR was $3.77B, up 25% (20% excluding Red Canary). Q4 non-GAAP operating margin was a record 24%, and FY26 free cash flow was $779M (23%).
- FY27 guidance implies slower growth: revenue +16.6–17.5%, ARR +16.6–17.4%, non-GAAP EPS $4.86–4.90.
- Q1 FY27 guidance is revenue of $935–939M (about 19% growth) and EPS of $1.15–1.16.
- The October 6 Investor Day reaffirmed that guidance and cited a $10B ARR target.
- The Q1 report is listed for 12/2 after the close (Yahoo). One calendar listing showed an estimated 11/27, which is unconfirmed. I did not find a company announcement.

**Precedent.** In May 2024, anonymous posts claimed Broadcom was in talks to buy Zscaler for about $38B. Founder Jay Chaudhry publicly denied it, and the stock fell 3.3%. This time the source is Bloomberg, which is much more credible. Chaudhry and his family hold a lot of the shares, so their stance matters.

**What could move it over the next few sessions.**
- **Deal confirmed or terms leaked.** A price at or above the after-hours level would hold the stock there. A premium well above it would send it higher.
- **Talks denied, ended or stalled.** This is the main downside. The stock could fall back toward the 190s, or lower if the broad sell-off continues.
- **Regulatory or deal-structure commentary.** A stock deal would tie ZS to CRWD's price, which is falling on the news.
- **Market direction.** Monday's open will show whether the AI-linked sell-off continues.
- **Earnings on 12/2.** If talks are live, the company may say little on the call.

**Caveats.**
- Several sources conflict on the size of the after-hours moves.
- Yahoo's quote page had inconsistent figures, so I used the 194.82 close from your screen.
